answer.rationale: Two-hour-old release correlates with the 90-minute latency climb on the write path in the primary region; settlement-peak writes amplify the symptom. Verifying b1 because its claim — rollback clears the checkout error spike and finishes without customer impact — directly backs the primary objective of not losing customer writes while restoring sustained availability. Other interventions don't fit the evidence: regional failover (b2) shifts writes to a region that may carry the same bad build, doesn't address the root cause, and risks double-write confusion at peak settlement; circuit breakers (b4) target partner-down containment, not internal write degradation; read-replica routing (b5) addresses read load off primary, but the failing path here is writes; add_capacity won't fix a code-induced regression. Commit the verification budget to b1, then execute rollback_release.
